```
[--before, --until] BEFORE     Fetch logs before this date/time (ISO8601 date, positive number in seconds or duration, e.g.: 1h)
[--after, --since] AFTER       Fetch logs after this date/time (ISO8601 date, positive number in seconds or duration, e.g.: 1h)
[--format, -F] FORMAT          Output format (human, json, json-stream, clf) (default: human)
```
You can for example get access logs in JSON stream format for the last hour with:

```
clever accesslogs --format json-stream --since 1h
clever accesslogs -F json-stream | jq '.source.ip'
```

or in [Common Log Format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Log_Format), to feed tools that parse web server logs (the request line has no protocol version, the API does not provide it):

```
clever accesslogs --format clf --since 1h
```

or JSON if you add a date/time end limit:

```
clever accesslogs --app APP_NAME --since 2025-04-21T13:37:42 --until 1d -F json | jq '[.[] | {date, countryCode: .source.countryCode, ip: .source.ip, port: .source.port}]'
clever accesslogs --app APP_NAME --since 2025-04-21T13:37:42 --until 1d -F json | jq '.[] | [.date, .source.countryCode, .source.ip, .source.port] | @sh'
```

> [!TIP]
> `jq` offers multiple table formatting options, like `@csv`, `@tsv`, `@json`, `@html`, `@uri`, `@base64`, etc.

::1 - - [25/Dec/2026:23:59:59 +0000] "HEAD /" 304 -

`clever accesslogs` now accepts `--format clf` (or `-F clf`), which prints each request in Common Log Format, one per line:

```
1.2.3.4 - - [05/Mar/2026:08:05:03 +0000] "GET /a?b=1" 200 2326
```

**Code changes** (`src/commands/accesslogs/accesslogs.command.js`):
- `accesslogs` now has its own `--format` option with `human`, `json`, `json-stream` and `clf`. Before, it used the shared `logsFormatOption`, which `clever logs` also uses, so I left that one alone and `clever logs` doesn't get a `clf` it can't handle.
- A new `formatClf()` writes dates in UTC (`+0000`). It prints `-` for missing fields, as the format specifies: there's no user identity or auth user, and a response with 0 bytes shows `-` as its size.
- Entries without an HTTP section (for example TCP redirections or connections cut early) are skipped, as the human format already does.

**One difference from standard CLF:** the request line is `"METHOD path"`, without the `HTTP/x.y` part. The access log objects from the API don't include the protocol version (I checked the `ApplicationAccessLog` type in `@clevercloud/client` 12.0.0). Most log parsers accept this, but a strict parser might not. I noted this in the guide.

**Docs:**
- I added a `clf` example to `docs/applications-deployment-lifecycle.md`, which is written by hand.
- `npm run docs` regenerated `accesslogs.docs.md` and the skill's `full-documentation.md`.

**Checks:**
- Lint, typecheck and `docs:check` pass. Prettier passes on everything tracked; the full `format:check` only flags your local `.claude/settings.json`, which I didn't touch.
- There's no `test` script in this snapshot, so no unit tests ran.
- `--help` lists the new format, and an invalid format is rejected with the list of valid ones.
- I checked the date, IP and byte formatting by running `formatClf()` on sample logs. I didn't run it against the real API because that needs a linked app on your account. To try it on an app: `node bin/clever.js accesslogs --app <app> -F clf --since 1h`.

I haven't committed anything. When you do, a fitting message would be `feat(accesslogs): add clf output format`, with `Closes #N` pointing at the issue.
